description: Day-to-day problems of people caring for dogs, cats and other pets: feeding, vet care, health records, medication, training, sitters, walking and travel.

items.title: Not knowing if the pet was fed
items.problem: In a household with several people, nobody is sure whether the dog or cat already ate, so the pet gets fed twice or skipped entirely.
items.who: families and roommates sharing a pet
items.workaround: group chat messages, a whiteboard on the fridge, or asking the pet's begging behaviour

items.title: Overwhelming pet food choices
items.problem: Choosing the right food takes days or months because there is no easy way to filter brands by the pet's age, allergies, breed and budget.
items.who: new pet owners and owners of pets with sensitivities
items.workaround: reading forum threads and asking the vet or pet store staff
items.source_quote: taking days to months to find the right food as there is no easy way to filter and narrow down relevant information

items.title: Running out of pet food unexpectedly
items.problem: The bag of kibble or box of litter runs out on a night when stores are closed, because nobody tracks consumption against what is left.
items.workaround: subscription deliveries that arrive too early or too late; emergency store runs

items.title: Portion sizes for weight management
items.problem: Owners are told the pet is overweight but cannot work out how many grams per meal to give across kibble, wet food and treats, and lose track of what treats added up during the day.
items.who: owners of overweight dogs and cats
items.workaround: guessing from the bag chart, measuring cups

items.title: Food transition schedules
items.problem: Switching a pet to a new food needs a gradual ratio change over 7-10 days, and owners forget which day they are on and cause stomach upsets.
items.workaround: sticky note on the food bin

items.title: Which human foods are toxic
items.problem: In the moment a pet grabs a grape, an onion scrap or a lily leaf, owners scramble to find out whether it is dangerous and how much is too much for the pet's weight.
items.workaround: frantic web searches, calling the vet or a poison hotline

items.title: Vaccination records not on hand
items.problem: Kennels, groomers, daycares and trainers ask for proof of vaccinations and owners cannot find the paper certificate or the vet email, and get turned away.
items.who: owners using boarding, grooming and daycare services
items.workaround: phone photos of certificates, calling the vet to re-send
items.source_quote: helps ensure you never get turned away at the kennel or groomer again

items.title: Medical history scattered across vets
items.problem: After moving or switching clinics, the pet's history is split between old clinics, emergency hospitals and paper printouts, so each new vet starts from scratch.
items.who: owners who have moved or used multiple clinics
items.workaround: requesting record transfers by fax or email, keeping a folder
items.source_quote: digitize, store, and share your pet's complete medical history, including vaccinations, medications, weight, and vet notes

items.title: Missing booster and deworming dates
items.problem: Annual boosters, rabies renewals and quarterly dewormers slip past because the only reminder is a postcard from the vet that gets lost.
items.workaround: vet reminder postcards and calendar entries
items.source_quote: set automated reminders for upcoming booster shots, deworming schedules, and vet appointments

items.title: Forgetting what to ask the vet
items.problem: Owners notice small concerns for weeks, then forget them in the exam room, and afterwards cannot recall what the vet actually said.
items.workaround: notes app, asking the vet to write it down

items.title: Interpreting vet advice given by chat
items.problem: Telehealth and clinic chat replies use clinical shorthand and owners struggle to understand what to actually do next.
items.who: owners using telehealth or clinic messaging
items.workaround: searching terms online, calling the clinic back
items.source_quote: interpreting veterinary advice on chat, or rescheduling appointments

items.title: Rescheduling vet appointments by phone
items.problem: Changing a vet appointment means calling during business hours, waiting on hold and taking whatever slot is offered.
items.source_quote: problems managing multiple pets, interpreting veterinary advice on chat, or rescheduling appointments

items.title: Pet health records without accounts
items.problem: Owners distrust cloud pet apps that require sign-up and subscriptions, and lose their data when the app shuts down or the plan lapses.
items.source_quote: works without an account, without a server, and without a subscription

items.title: Emergency vet decision at 2am
items.problem: When a pet vomits or limps at night, owners cannot tell whether it can wait until morning or needs the expensive emergency hospital right now.

items.title: Finding a vet with open appointments
items.problem: Clinics are booked out for weeks and new-patient waitlists are long, so owners phone clinic after clinic looking for anyone who can see the pet soon.
items.who: owners in areas with vet shortages

items.title: Tracking daily medication doses
items.problem: Pets on twice-daily pills, ear drops or insulin get double-dosed or missed because caregivers cannot remember whether the morning dose was given.
items.who: owners of chronically ill or senior pets
items.workaround: pill organisers, notes on the counter
items.source_quote: manage your pet's medications and treatments with smart reminders and detailed tracking

items.title: Flea, tick and heartworm renewals
items.problem: Monthly preventatives are applied late or skipped because the 30-day cycle drifts and each pet in the house is on a different date.

items.title: Monitoring a senior pet's quality of life
items.problem: Owners of aging pets cannot tell whether bad days are becoming more frequent, making end-of-life decisions feel like guesswork.
items.who: owners of elderly or terminally ill pets
items.workaround: memory and gut feeling; printed quality-of-life scales
items.source_quote: allows owners to record whether a pet had a good, neutral, or bad day

items.title: Spotting gradual weight changes
items.problem: Slow weight loss or gain in a cat or dog goes unnoticed for months because the pet is only weighed at the annual visit.
items.source_quote: keeps your vaccination record, medication schedule, vet visit note, and weight log organized

items.title: Litter box habits as health signal
items.problem: Changes in a cat's urination or stool frequency are early signs of urinary blockage or kidney disease, but in multi-cat homes nobody knows which cat did what.
items.workaround: separating cats, expensive smart litter boxes

items.title: Logging symptoms for the vet
items.problem: When asked how often the dog has been vomiting or scratching, owners can only guess because they never wrote incidents down with dates.
items.who: owners of pets with recurring issues
items.source_quote: track incidents, weight, height & length, medications, allergies, expenses

items.title: Elimination-diet allergy detective work
items.problem: Figuring out which ingredient triggers a pet's itching requires weeks of controlled feeding and correlating flare-ups, which owners cannot keep straight.
items.who: owners of pets with food allergies

items.title: Vetting an unknown pet sitter
items.problem: Sitters on marketplace apps are effectively strangers with no verified references, insurance or licences, and owners have no way to check beyond star ratings.
items.source_quote: random people with no checks on references, insurances or licences to have a dog sitting business

items.title: No proof the walk happened
items.problem: Owners pay for a 30-minute walk or a drop-in visit and have no evidence the sitter actually came, stayed the full time or fed the pet.
items.who: owners using dog walkers and drop-in sitters

items.title: Sitter lost the dog, no help finding it
items.problem: When a sitter lets a dog escape, owners are far away and the platform offers little coordinated help searching, contacting shelters or alerting neighbours.
items.workaround: social media posts, lost-pet flyers, shelter calls
items.source_quote: dogs escaped and weren't found until days later... Rover didn't do enough to help when the dogs went missing

items.title: Sitter mixing incompatible dogs
items.problem: Owners cannot see which other animals a sitter is hosting at the same time, so small dogs end up housed with large unknown dogs.
items.who: owners boarding dogs in sitters' homes
items.workaround: asking the sitter directly and trusting the answer
items.source_quote: the dog walker from Rover was watching her dog and a mastiff at the same home

items.title: Strangers with home access
items.problem: Walkers and sitters need to enter the home unsupervised, and owners have no log of who came in, when, and whether anything went missing.
items.workaround: smart locks with one-time codes, cameras
items.source_quote: $5,000 was missing from her house after the dog walker she hired through Wag had entered her home

items.title: Per-booking fees and confusing messages
items.problem: Sitter platforms add a fee to every single booking and send overlapping emails and texts, so owners lose track of what is confirmed and what it costs.
items.workaround: taking the relationship off-platform once trusted
items.source_quote: admin fees of £6 for each individual booking and confusing communication with multiple emails and texts sent simultaneously

items.title: Handing over care instructions
items.problem: Every time a new sitter or friend takes the pet, the owner re-types feeding amounts, medication, quirks, vet contact and emergency wishes from memory.
items.who: anyone who leaves pets with others
items.workaround: long text messages, printed sheets on the counter

items.title: Sitter unsure of emergency authority
items.problem: If a pet falls ill while the owner is unreachable, the sitter does not know which vet to use, what the owner will pay for, or who can authorise treatment.
items.workaround: verbal instructions, a note with the vet's number

items.title: Finding a reliable last-minute walker
items.problem: When the owner gets stuck late at work, there is no trusted person available on short notice to let the dog out.
items.workaround: begging neighbours, on-demand walker apps with unknown walkers

items.title: Sitter feedback not visible to owners
items.problem: Sitters leave notes about difficult pets that owners never see, so owners cannot correct behaviour or understand why bookings get declined.
items.who: owners of reactive or anxious pets
items.source_quote: When you post feedback on a dog can the owners view it?

items.title: Puppy potty-training timing
items.problem: New puppy owners cannot remember when the puppy last peed, ate or drank, so they miss the window and get accidents indoors.
items.workaround: timers, paper logs, taking the puppy out constantly
items.source_quote: surprise puddles and accidents on the floor

items.title: Inconsistent commands between family members
items.problem: Each person in the house uses different words and rules for the dog, so training stalls and the dog gets confused.
items.workaround: arguments, a list on the fridge

items.title: Tracking training progress over weeks
items.problem: Owners cannot tell whether recall, leash pulling or separation anxiety are actually improving because they never record sessions or outcomes.

items.title: Barking complaints while owner is away
items.problem: Owners only learn their dog barks all day when a neighbour complains, and have no way to know when or what triggers it.
items.source_quote: early morning barking alarms, destroyed belongings

items.title: Behavior problems leading to rehoming
items.problem: Owners struggle with destruction, barking or aggression without structured guidance and end up giving pets back to shelters.
items.source_quote: animal behavior problems such as damaging or barking accounts for 29.4 percent of cancellations

items.title: Cat scratching and litter avoidance triggers
items.problem: Cat owners cannot pinpoint why a cat suddenly stopped using the box or started scratching furniture, since triggers are spread over days.
items.workaround: trial and error with litter types and locations

items.title: Socialisation checklist for puppies
items.problem: The critical socialisation window closes at about 16 weeks and owners do not know which experiences (surfaces, sounds, people, vehicles) they have covered.

items.title: Dog not getting enough exercise
items.problem: Owners lose track of how much the dog actually walked this week versus what its breed and age need, and the dog acts out.

items.title: Finding safe off-leash areas
items.problem: Owners do not know which nearby parks allow off-leash dogs, when they are crowded, or whether reactive dogs are present.

items.title: Hot pavement and weather risks
items.problem: Owners do not realise pavement is hot enough to burn paws or the day is too hot or cold for a walk until the dog is hurt.

items.title: Pet-friendly places while travelling
items.problem: Finding hotels, restaurants and beaches that genuinely allow pets, with their size limits and fees, takes many calls and out-of-date listings.

items.title: Flight and border paperwork for pets
items.problem: Each airline and country has different vaccination, microchip and health-certificate rules with strict timing windows, and one missed step strands the pet.
items.who: owners relocating or flying with pets

items.title: Meeting other dog owners nearby
items.problem: Owners of a single dog have no easy way to find compatible playmates or walking partners close by for socialisation.
items.who: owners of young or lonely dogs
items.source_quote: allowing dog owners to connect and build trusted support networks

items.title: Surprise vet bills
items.problem: Treatment costs are unclear until the invoice arrives, and owners cannot compare prices or budget for likely annual expenses.
items.who: all pet owners, especially on tight budgets
items.workaround: asking for estimates, care credit cards

items.title: Pet insurance claim paperwork
items.problem: Submitting claims requires itemised invoices and medical notes that owners have to chase from the clinic, then wait weeks for reimbursement.

items.title: Tracking total pet spending
items.problem: Food, litter, vet, grooming and sitters are spread across many stores and cards, so owners have no idea what the pet costs per month.
items.source_quote: track incidents, weight, height & length, medications, allergies, expenses, pet boarding

items.title: Managing several pets' schedules
items.problem: With multiple pets each on different food, meds and vet dates, owners mix up which animal is due for what.
items.source_quote: Specific pain points include problems managing multiple pets

items.title: Co-parenting a pet across two homes
items.problem: Separated couples or friends sharing custody of a pet lose track of whose week it is, what was fed and what the vet said.

items.title: Lost pet with nowhere to broadcast
items.problem: When a pet goes missing, owners must post separately on multiple social groups, shelters and poster sites, while finders have no single place to check.
items.workaround: flyers, neighbourhood social groups, microchip registries

items.title: Grooming and nail-trim intervals
items.problem: Owners forget when nails were last clipped, ears cleaned or the coat brushed, and only notice when the dog is clicking on the floor or matted.
items.who: owners of long-coated or indoor pets

items.title: Small-animal cage and tank upkeep
items.problem: Rabbit, hamster, reptile and fish owners forget water changes, substrate swaps, UV bulb replacements and enclosure temperature checks.
items.who: owners of small animals, reptiles and fish

items.title: Shedding and cleaning routines
items.problem: Seasonal shedding overwhelms the home and owners cannot predict when to increase brushing or which products actually reduce hair on clothes.
items.source_quote: dog owners frequently deal with excessive shedding, with dog hair accumulating on their clothes
